newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's loses $1 bln duty per year to smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's loses $1 bln duty per year to smuggling.

text.p: Colombia is losing almost $1 billion a year in import duties -- equivalent to about 1 percent of gross domestic product -- as a result of smuggling, President Ernesto Samper said Wednesday.
The total value of goods smuggled into Colombia is estimated to be about $5 billion per year -- much of that brought in by drug traffickers looking for ways to launder their illicit earnings.

"The explosive mixture of a strengthening peso currency, drug-traffickers eager to launder money, the actions of corrupt officials and unscrupulous buyers have plunged certain manufacturing sectors into deep crisis," Samper said at an official ceremony to swear in Gustavo Cote, the new head of Colombia's customs agency.

He said goods smuggled into the country accounted for almost half of all foreign goods coming into Colombia. According to government estimates 70 percent of all cigarettes smoked in Colombia are contraband, costing the nation $120 million in lost import duties.
Other sectors also hard hit by smuggling are the domestic clothes, liquor, leather and shoe industries, according to recent studies by the National Industrialists Association (ANDI).
So far this year Colombian customs agents have confiscated $40 million in contraband goods.

The former National Tax and Customs Department (DIAN) has now been split into two separate agencies in a bid to boost efficiency and last month Congress passed a law to impose prison sentences on those found guilty of smuggling.
